etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Anglo-Norman peremptorie, parentorie et al. (Modern French péremptoire), and its source, Latin peremptōrius (“deadly; precluding debate, decisive”), from perimō (“destroy, thwart”), from per- (“thorough”) + emō (“to obtain, buy”).
senses: (law) Precluding debate or expostulation; not admitting of question or appeal.
(law) Of a date or deadline, absolutely requiring compliance or attendance; brooking no further delay; proceeding whether a party attends or not; final.
(law) A challenge to the admission of a juror, without the challenger needing to show good cause.
